citations.author: Paul Graham

citations.title: Default Alive or Default Dead?
citations.author: Paul Graham

citations.title: Startups in 13 Sentences
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: February 2009. The most compressed statement of the YC canon: launch fast, make a few users love you, spend little, understand your users.

citations.title: How to Start a Startup
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: March 2005. The pre-YC founding text: good people, make something customers want, spend as little as possible.

citations.title: Before the Startup
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: October 2014. Startups are so counterintuitive that trusting instincts trained elsewhere fails; expertise in startups is not what matters — users are.

citations.title: The 18 Mistakes That Kill Startups
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: October 2006. Enumerates the recurring killers; concludes they are all proxies for a single mistake — not making something users want.

citations.title: The Equity Equation
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: July 2007. The 1/(1-n) rule: give up n% of the company only when the trade makes the remaining (1-n) worth more than the whole was before.

citations.title: How to Raise Money
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: September 2013. Breadth-first fundraising weighted by expected value, get commitments in writing, and get back to work — fundraising is not the company.

citations.title: How to Get Startup Ideas
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: November 2012. The best ideas are noticed, not made up: live in the future, build what is missing, prefer a deep well (a few users who need it urgently) to a shallow lake.

citations.title: Ramen Profitable
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: July 2009. Covering the founders' living expenses from revenue changes the fundraising power balance and removes the ticking clock.

citations.title: How Not to Die
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: August 2007. Startups rarely die in mid-keystroke — they die because the founders give up or run out of money while demoralized.

citations.title: Relentlessly Resourceful
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: March 2009. The two-word test for good founders: relentlessly resourceful — the opposite of hapless.

citations.title: Be Good
citations.author: Paul Graham
citations.note: April 2008. Benevolence as strategy: being genuinely good to users compounds into growth, morale, and help from outside.

citations.title: First Round Review
citations.author: First Round Capital
citations.note: Long-form operator interviews and playbooks; the strongest open corpus on management and company building between seed and scale.

citations.title: The Struggle
citations.author: Ben Horowitz (Andreessen Horowitz)
citations.note: 2012. The definitive essay on the psychological low points of running a company — the Struggle is where greatness comes from, and everyone goes through it.

citations.title: Startup Playbook
citations.author: Sam Altman
citations.note: 2015. A single-sitting synthesis of the YC canon: a great idea, a great product, a great team, and great execution.

citations.title: Steve Blank — customer development corpus
citations.author: Steve Blank
citations.note: Origin of customer development and 'get out of the building' — the empirical method underneath the lean-startup movement.

citations.title: Stripe Atlas Guides

citations.title: The Holloway Guide to Equity Compensation
citations.author: Joshua Levy, Joe Wallin, et al. (Holloway)
citations.note: The most complete open reference on startup equity comp: options vs RSUs, 409A and strike prices, exercise windows, and tax pitfalls. Cited by lib/openstartup/equityComp.ts.

citations.title: Rewarding Talent — the Index Ventures option-plan handbook
citations.author: Index Ventures
citations.note: Published benchmarks and conventions for employee option pools and grant sizing, US and Europe. Cited by lib/openstartup/equityComp.ts.

citations.author: Delaware Division of Corporations

Law § 195(1)(a) (written notice at the time of hiring, in English and the employee's primary language: rate or rates of pay and basis, allowances claimed, the regular pay day, employer name and any “doing business as” names, physical and mailing address, telephone number; signed acknowledgment retained six years), § 195(3) (wage statement with every payment of wages listing dates covered, names, address and phone, rates, gross wages, deductions, and net wages)

citations.title: RCW 49.62.020: Noncompetition covenants — validity — notice
citations.locator: RCW 49.62.020(1)(a) (written disclosure of the covenant's terms no later than acceptance of the offer; independent consideration if entered after employment begins), (1)(b) (void and unenforceable unless the employee's annualized earnings from the enforcing party exceed $100,000, the statutory base adjusted annually for inflation under RCW 49.62.040), (1)(c) (a laid-off employee must receive base-salary compensation for the enforcement period, less subsequent earnings), (2) (duration over 18 months presumed unreasonable absent clear and convincing evidence)
citations.note: Official legislative text; verified live 2026-10-14. The operative dollar threshold is the inflation-adjusted figure the Department of Labor & Industries publishes each year, not the $100,000 statutory base.

citations.note: Statutory text verified live 2026-10-14 via the LII U.S. Code mirror (registry precedent: usc-irc-421).

citations.title: 17 U.S.C. § 101: Definitions (work made for hire)
citations.locator: 17 U.S.C. § 101 “work made for hire”: (1) a work prepared by an employee within the scope of employment; (2) a specially ordered or commissioned work only within nine enumerated categories (contribution to a collective work, part of a motion picture or other audiovisual work, translation, supplementary work, compilation, instructional text, test, answer material for a test, atlas) and only if the parties expressly agree in a written instrument signed by them
citations.note: Statutory text verified live 2026-10-14 via the LII U.S. Code mirror (registry precedent: usc-irc-421).
